newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Chase eyes Brazil's Vale sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Chase eyes Brazil's Vale sell-off.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Corp's Brazil unit has begun talks with investors eyeing the privatization of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) next year, said the bank's president Patric Morin Jr.
Morin said the bank wants to participate in Vale's sell-off as an advisor or as a direct investor, although he noted the company's privatization will require a large amount of cash.
"We may invest ourselves, but Vale's sell-off will require large investments. We will analyse the opportunity, although I think it is difficult," he said.
Morin said he expects Vale to be privatized in the first half of 1997, instead of the third quarter as government officials planned.
He also said he agreed with Vale's privatization model, noting that a sale exclusively via public offering as suggested by politicians would reduce government receipts in the sale.
"I have no doubts that a sale via public offering would reduce by 20 percent to 30 percent what could be raised with the sale," Morin said.

Earlier today a spokesman for the Planning Ministry said the government does not intend to change the privatization model, adding that a proposal by Lower House president Luiz Eduardo Magalhaes that the company be sold entirely via public offering was unacceptable.
"That was never the government's idea and the government won't alter its model," the spokesman said.
The government plans a 40-45 percent block sale of voting shares in the first quarter, followed by offers to employees and to the public.
Although in favor of Vale's sell-off plan, Morin criticized rules restricting the participation of major producers, consumers and traders of iron ore.
The chief for Chase Brazil unit also said he does not see high global demand for Vale shares.
"Many foreign players limit their investment in Brazil in terms of region. Also investment in mining today is not so attractive," he said.

Besides CVRD, Chase is also closely watching Brazil's electrical and telecommunications sectors, particularly the upcoming privatizations of Sao Paulo power firms and the country's Band B cellular services.
Regarding Band B, Chase is currently an advisor and arranger for a consortium made up of AT&T do Brasil, Globopar and other investors to bid for a concession to operate cellular services.
Morin said this consortium may seek some $1.0 billion in funds to invest in Band B.
